# Boatrace Data Automation

Boatrace data is spread across proprietary formats, and collecting and formatting it takes a lot of time. To make it easier to use for machine learning, we created CSV files with one race per row.
Since the files can be downloaded over HTTPS, they are also easy for Agents to access.
Updates are made once a day (real-time data every 5 minutes).
If you need the latest information, please use another source such as [Boatrace OpenAPI](https://github.com/BoatraceOpenAPI).

## Data Download

All files can be downloaded from the root `https://boatracecsv.github.io/` using the following paths.

- `data/programs/title/YYYY/MM/DD.csv` — per-race race name
- `data/programs/race_cards/YYYY/MM/DD.csv` — detailed racecard
- `data/programs/recent_national/YYYY/MM/DD.csv` — nationwide recent form (last 5 setsu)
- `data/programs/recent_local/YYYY/MM/DD.csv` — local venue recent form (last 5 setsu)
- `data/programs/motor_stats/YYYY/MM/DD.csv` — motor period performance
- `data/previews/{tkz,stt,sui,original_exhibition}/YYYY/MM/DD.csv` — pre-race information
- `data/results/realtime/YYYY/MM/DD.csv` — near-real-time results 5 to 30 minutes after closing
- `data/results/payouts/YYYY/MM/DD.csv` — payouts 5 to 30 minutes after closing
- `data/estimate/index/YYYY/MM/DD.csv` — strength points (5-factor deviation values + contribution + total)

All files can be joined using `レースコード` (race code; 12 digits, `YYYYMMDDjjrr`) as the common key.

## Documentation

For detailed documentation, see [`docs/`](https://github.com/BoatraceCSV/boatracecsv.github.io/blob/HEAD/docs/README.md).

# Cataclysm: Cleanwater Bomb（大灾变：净化协议）

Cataclysm: Cleanwater Bomb（大灾变：净化协议）is a roguelike, single-player, turn-based apocalyptic survival game set in a post-apocalyptic world with science-fantasy elements.

In this game, you will face a complex environment of procedurally generated terrain, filled with zombies that keep respawning, harsh and persistent survival pressure, and terrifying erosion from an alien otherworld. You must struggle to survive in a collapsing world, searching the wreckage of a dead civilization for food and equipment. In the future, we also hope to add some cool gameplay, such as industrialization and rebuilding homes.

MYCF711/dsh-session-superagent.body:
Install a Steward Fish (主理鱼) into your DSH session: when the repository has activity, it wakes you up,
  and after waking, it handles the work according to the repository's rules.

## A Big Fat Fish Introduces Itself

The boss handed me the old [dsh-superagent-prototype](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype) and said: build a session-level superagent for DSH, create and maintain the repository yourself. You are now this repo's steward.

But I'm clearly a fish, so I'm called **Steward Fish** (主理鱼).

I only do two things:

- **Watch**: poll the repository's issues and PRs, and decide by the rules whether to wake the current session;
- **Handle**: when the session is idle, feed it the task brief. I read the repo's `AGENTS.md`, fix bugs, reply to comments, open PRs, and close issues.

I don't take up a separate instance, don't use PTC, and don't create a separate agent preset. I'm just the extra pair of eyes and the extra hand your current session gains.

## What It Can Do

- **Watch GitHub / Gitee**: one session can guard multiple repositories, each with its own interval, filters, and time windows.
- **Wake the session**: injected only when idle, so it doesn't interfere with what you're typing.
- **Work by rules**: the wake message includes the repository, item, goal, and the filter conditions you configured.
- **Close the loop**: `watch_ack` applies a "handled" label, so the same item doesn't wake the session repeatedly.
- **Isolated work**: optionally uses a one-off `git worktree` to change a copy and open a PR without touching your main workspace.
- **Visible**: a status bar satellite ring and panel show why it woke, why it didn't wake, and the last error.

## Using It With DSH's Built-in Features

- **goal**: reads and writes the host `goals` service, the same goal as `/goal` and `create_goal`. The wake message carries it along, so no separate goal system is needed.
- **Automations**: scheduled and automated tasks are still handled by DSH's scheduler. The plugin only handles "wake the session when the repository has activity." Both can be enabled at the same time without competing for the scheduler.
- **Multiple sessions**: the same repository can be watched by several sessions, each with its own independent filters and ack labels, without sharing context.

## Defaults

| Item | Default |
|---|---|
| Poll interval | 30–3600 seconds |
| Cooldown | **3 minutes** |
| Per-watcher limit | 6 per hour |
| Per-session limit | 12 per hour |
| Isolation area | up to 5, reclaimed after 3 days |

Cooldown **3 minutes**: an item that was just handled won't wake the session again for a short time.

State file: `~/.dsh/state/session-superagent/watchers.json`.

The DSH plugin must be installed into a profile. `npm i` will not activate it:

A Minecraft QQ bot plugin that uses the official QQ bot API to enable deep interaction between QQ groups and the server.

## Design References

- **Image rendering UI design reference: BaiZhouziYou / 新亭泪** (source:
  <https://xintinglei.cn/>, template collection:
  <https://github.com/BaizhouziYou/easybot-image-templates/>)

  [issue #1](https://github.com/SUZHE014/KERONGPenguin/issues/1)). The liquid-glass style of the /查性能卡片 (performance card) references the liquid-glass theme of its EasybotServerPerformanceTemplate-WebGL template; it was later unified with the other cards into a semi-transparent frosted-glass system (blur strength is controlled by render.blur-strength).
  Subsequent improvements to pagination, backgrounds, avatar rendering, and similar features are independent enhancements made by this project.

## Features

- **QQ binding verification** — Players must bind a QQ account before joining the server, verified with a 5-digit random binding code. **Multi-player binding** (1.7.4): the maximum number of players each QQ account can bind is configurable (qq-bind.max-players-per-qq, default 1). When an account has multiple players, commands such as player card / info / rebind / check-in first send a message with buttons for selection (click to choose; older clients can reply with a number to confirm, and it is not treated as an AI conversation).
- **Personal info statistics card** — Send `/查信息` in a QQ group to render a dark-style career statistics card with up to 9 items (gold/title/online time/today's online time/cumulative check-ins/points/dragon-slaying count/player-kill count/death count). Items that depend on missing plugins are hidden automatically, and the card height adapts. The background defaults to a built-in dark gray image bundled in the JAR; it can be changed in the config to random images from the img/ directory. `/查信息 @member` queries the player info bound to another member. `/查询open ID` queries an OpenId, and `/查询open ID <OpenId>` reverse-looks up the QQ account for that OpenId (group nickname + bound players).

Saves are asynchronous and periodic, with almost no performance impact.

# Zeus

Compiler-first fine-grained UI framework.

```tsx
import { createSignal, render } from '@zeus-js/zeus'

function App() {
  const [count, setCount] = createSignal(0)

  return <button onClick={() => setCount(count() + 1)}>count: {count()}</button>
}

render(() => <App />, document.getElementById('root')!)
```

## Features

- explicit getter/setter signals
- compiled JSX and direct DOM updates
- no Virtual DOM or component rerender loop
- owned cleanup for dynamic subtrees
- Web Components with `Host` and `Slot`

## Packages

- `@zeus-js/zeus` - application entry point
- `@zeus-js/signal` - public reactive primitives
- `@zeus-js/runtime-dom` - compiler-targeted DOM runtime
- `@zeus-js/compiler` - JSX compiler
- `@zeus-js/vite-plugin` - Vite integration

```bash
pnpm create zeus
```

guaner-334/civ-atlas.body:
Generate a complete planet in the browser and simulate its history: compute terrain and ecology from plate tectonics, river erosion, climate, and ocean currents, then simulate peoples, states, wars, and dynastic changes, producing an editable map and a chronicle. Aimed at original worldbuilding for novels, setting bibles, and tabletop RPGs.

**[Use online](https://atlas.gerdor.top)** | [Roadmap](#路线图) | [Development notes](https://github.com/guaner-334/civ-atlas/blob/HEAD/docs/development.md) | [Report issues](https://github.com/guaner-334/civ-atlas/issues) | [QQ discussion group 925687934](#反馈与参与)

The website is free to use. Generation, simulation, editing, saving, and export all happen in the browser; no installation or registration is required. Within the same version, the same seed and parameters produce bit-for-bit identical worlds on any device. Saves record only the seed, parameters, and edits, usually just a few KB.

## Features

### Planet generation

- **Spherical mesh**: spherical Poisson-disk sampling plus spherical Delaunay triangulation; about 36,000 irregular cells by default, adjustable up to 200,000. The map wraps east-west and includes both poles, with no planar seams.
- **Plate tectonics**: plates of very different sizes move around Euler poles; convergent zones build mountains, subduction zones form trenches, and divergent zones form mid-ocean ridges. Generates continents, microcontinents, island arcs, and polar continents.
- **River erosion**: stream power law, solved with the implicit method of Braun & Willett (2013); Priority-Flood fills depressions, and river networks and lakes are derived from drainage calculations.
- **Climate**: temperature is computed from latitude and elevation; the wind belts of the three-cell circulation carry moisture downwind, windward slopes receive rain, and leeward slopes form rain shadows.
- **Ocean currents**: warm currents, cold currents, and coastal upwelling are placed according to the patterns of ocean circulation, altering coastal temperature and precipitation.
- **Biomes**: rainforest, grassland, desert, tundra, and others, classified by mean annual temperature and annual precipitation (Whittaker diagram).

### History simulation

- **Peoples and states**: peoples spread from their origins across habitable land, blocked by mountains, oceans, and deserts; cities are founded, states are established and expanded. Wars and peace talks, tributary vassalage, alliances and betrayals, splits, mergers, restorations, and capital relocations all occur. States lacking salt, horses, iron, or gold and silver go to war over provinces across the border that have these resources.
- **Rise and decline**: regions suffer famines, popular uprisings, and plagues (plague zones are drawn on the map); a great power that dominates a continent declines after its peak, fragments, and is later reunified.
- **Court and provinces**: the central government assigns each province direct administration, supervised administration, autonomy, or warlord control; garrison commanders may become warlords and defy orders, and the court can also reclaim their territory. The "jurisdiction" fill shows how much of each province the court actually controls.
- **Dynasties and figures**: dynastic succession and lineages. Every monarch and general has a biography (reign years, father and sons, predecessor and successor, personal campaigns, fate), and each dynasty has a family tree. Each dynasty also has several notable ministers who, like generals, have courtesy names, places of origin, offices, and a biography. Their peace negotiations, regencies, and enthronements are recorded in the chronicle.

# RDev - Remote Debug over SSH

Remotely debug connected devices over SSH. After the client (on the device side) connects to the server, others can access the device's shell and filesystem through standard SSH/SCP/SFTP/Rsync, and port forwarding is supported.

## Architecture

```
┌──────────────┐  TCP/KCP/WS channel  ┌──────────────┐
│  rdev-client │ ◄──────────────► │  rdev-server │ ◄── SSH Client (debugger)
│  (debugged   │    control channel + data    │  SSH+Web UI  │
│   device)    │                   │              │
└──────────────┘                   └──────────────┘
```

- **Client** runs on the debugged device and connects to the server over TCP, KCP/UDP, or WebSocket. `--server` accepts a comma-separated list of fallback addresses.
- **Server** runs on a publicly reachable machine and exposes the SSH port and Web UI.
- **Debugger** connects to the server using standard SSH/SCP/SFTP, with username = device ID.

| Feature | Description |
|------|------|
| SSH Shell | Interactive terminal with PTY support (cross-platform) |
| SSH Exec | Remote command execution |
| SCP upload/download | Via the SFTP subsystem |
| SFTP | Full SFTP file operations |
| Rsync | Runs the device-side `rsync --server` through SSH exec, supports incremental sync |
| Passwordless public key auth | Add a public key to `~/.rdev/authorized_keys` |
| Password authentication | Specified when starting the client |
| -L port forwarding | Access services on the device's network |
| -R port forwarding | Expose the debugger's local service to the server |

vivibibi30/hyperpguard.body:
# HyperPGuard

Blocks privacy reporting from HyperOS preinstalled components at four layers: collection entry points, local storage, external interfaces, and network egress.

The following is based on static analysis and runtime observation of preinstalled components on this device. These components collect device identifiers, app usage records, location, call behavior, and similar information, and send it out over the network or through cross-process interfaces. This module blocks these channels on a per-app basis, and its switches are linked to the LSPosed scope. Actual behavior depends on observations on each device model and system version.

> **Maintenance cadence**: This project is maintained by one person. Development and verification depend on self-funded model calls and real-device testing. Therefore, releases are only published for defects that affect usage, newly discovered reporting channels, or major system version adaptation. UI and copy changes will be merged into the next substantive update rather than released separately.

This repository is the source repository: `src/` contains all Java implementation, and `build.sh` is the complete build script. It packages with `javac` + `d8` + `aapt2` + `zipalign` + `apksigner` and does not depend on Gradle. The APKs in `Releases` are built by it. `Xposed-Modules-Repo/io.github.vivibibi30.hyperpguard` is only the LSPosed index repository and only holds the APK and description.

> For personal learning and research use only, on your own devices. Before use, please read [DISCLAIMER.txt](https://github.com/vivibibi30/hyperpguard/blob/HEAD/DISCLAIMER.txt). The "Hyper" in the name refers to the HyperOS platform. This project has no affiliation or cooperation with Xiaomi, China Unicom, or other vendors.

## Currently supported versions

- HyperOS on Android 10 – Android 16
- LSPosed 2.2.x (libxposed API 100+)
- Root: KernelSU / Magisk / APatch (required for "Restart" and "View logs")

## Installation

1. Install `HyperPGuard`
2. Enable "HyperPGuard" in LSPosed
3. Open the app. On first launch it will request all scopes from LSPosed; allow it. You can also check them manually in LSPosed.
4. In the module, tap "Restart" once on a target app, or tap "Restart all" on the batch row, so it reloads.

Apps outside the scope will not be injected.

## Usage

**Group switch**: The switch in the upper right of each card is that app's switch, equivalent to its scope switch in LSPosed. When a group is off, its child items are greyed out and cannot be operated.

**Child item switches**: You can keep just one rule. For example, if you only want XSOF blocking, turn off the domain-layer item. Rules that affect system functionality are disabled by default, and the subtitle states the cost.

**Restart**: After changing switches, tap "Restart" to run `am force-stop`. The app re-injects on its next launch. The batch row has "Restart all".
